newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu to hold summit with Egypt's Mubarak.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu to hold summit with Egypt's Mubarak.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will meet Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Tuesday to try and break a two-month deadlock in Middle East peacemaking, Netanyahu's office said on Thursday.
"The meeting will take place according to a proposal by Mubarak aimed at exchanging ideas ... to further the political process in the region," Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak said in a statement.
"It is the intention of both sides to raise ideas in order to advance solutions to the present crisis," the statement said.
The meeting was due to take place in the Egyptian Red Sea resort town of Sharm el-Sheikh.

The statement said the meeting was arranged during a two-day flurry of Egyptian-Israeli contacts. Mubarak met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Cairo on Wednesday to discuss ways of reviving moribund talks.
The last time Netanyahu met Mubarak was in early March. It was their third meeting since Netanyahu took office last June.

Earlier on Thursday, sources close to Netanyahu accused Egypt of attempting to bypass Netanyahu by trying to set up a meeting between Mubarak and Israeli President Ezer Weizman, whose post is largely ceremonial.

Diplomatic sources said Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa would be in Israel on Monday. Bazak told Reuters it was likely Moussa would meet Netanyahu during his visit but said no meeting was set yet.

Peacemaking ground to a halt when Netanyahu ordered work to begin on a new Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem on March 18. Palestinians saw the move as an attempt to pre-empt future "final status" peace talks on the city's fate.
Netanyahu has said he is proud of the decision to build the 6,500-unit settlement and has refused PLO demands to halt its construction.
Israel occupied East Jerusalem in 1967 and claimed the whole city as its capital. The claim is not recognised internationally. Palestinians want East Jerusalem as capital of a future state.
